tasks.short: Develop solar installation procedures and safety or quality standards.

steps.what: Examine actual solar installation methods, hazards and quality failures
Find and read actual applicable installation instructions and safety or quality requirements
Develop safe operating methods, acceptance criteria and installation responsibilities
outputs: chosen solar installation methods and criteria

steps.what: Write standard operation procedures and quality or safety standards for solar installation work
inputs: chosen solar installation methods and criteria
outputs: solar installation procedure and standards draft

loop.purpose: Draft procedures from engineer-chosen safe methods and criteria
loop.input: Verified requirements, actual hazards and chosen methods and acceptance criteria
loop.check: Engineer checks sequence, responsibility, omitted hazards, changed safety meaning and unsupported thresholds against actual source requirements
loop.stop: Missing requirement or two failed revisions returns drafting to manual work
loop.why_not_simpler: Use controlled document headings and fixed requirement fields first; explanatory work instructions vary by installation method

steps.what: Check the final procedure and standards against actual work and release scope
inputs: solar installation procedure and standards draft
outputs: checked final installation procedure and standards

steps.what: Save the checked final installation procedure and standards revision
inputs: checked final installation procedure and standards

steps.what: Release the checked procedure revision to its authorised internal installation audience

tasks.design: Configure requirement search and controlled headings in {DOCS} first, then use a bounded draft for instructions based on the engineer's actual methods and criteria. The engineer inspects work, decides safety and quality requirements and checks the exact final revision before its separate save and release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures repeat source finding and explanatory writing across installation methods.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled source filters and bounded source-linked drafting can reduce retrieval and first-draft prose.
tasks.still_hard: Safe installation methods, acceptance limits and the adequacy of hazard controls require accountable engineering judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer understands the physical work and notices hazards omitted by a plausible instruction.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft writing; safety and release authority stay as actually delegated.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: controlled document search and source-linked language drafting can support procedures; they cannot establish safe methods or acceptance criteria.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual procedure and standards development through release by an engineer who actually holds that authority. Where another safety owner must approve, record that actual dependency and owner; do not treat their work as saved focal labour.

Manufacturer and requirement owners supply actual equipment identifier, instruction revision, requirement identifier and applicability. The engineer finds and reads them in s2, assesses hazards in s1 and creates methods and acceptance criteria in s3. Missing sources or uncertain applicability stay manual; the model never invents a limit.
Test native search and fixed controlled templates before custom code. Existing source retrieval earns no saving. Source reading remains within s2 and generated meaning correction remains within s4.

Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Save and release each retain their one percent share; s5 is the existing engineering check, not an added self-approval ceremony.
unknowns: Who holds actual safety-standard release authority?
How much procedure text is already reusable?
research_questions: Does drafting save time after checking every hazard, sequence and acceptance criterion against real work?

already_counted.description: Correct draft meaning and missing instructions within s4.

incremental.description: Maintain source links, controlled headings and drafting checks.

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked final installation procedure and standards, exact revision and document destination; edits void approval
s5 checked final installation procedure and standards, exact revision and authorised release scope; changes require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 20*0.25 retrieval + 24*0.40 prose = 14.6, minus 1.5 upkeep = 13.1. If only half the source retrieval and prose are eligible, 7.3 minus 1.5 = 5.8. Safety choices, inspection and release time stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyse solar-system thermal performance, stress or costs.

steps.what: Collect and verify actual thermal, stress or cost inputs for solar systems
Choose thermal, stress or cost reduction analysis methods and boundary conditions
Set up analysis cases in the engineering solver {OTHER} or calculation workbook
Interpret thermal, stress or cost analysis results and validate limitations
Write and check the actual solar analysis findings and source references
Save the checked final solar analysis findings

tasks.design: Use native input imports and reusable engineering case definitions in the solver {OTHER} and {SPREADSHEET}. The engineer checks actual input units and sources, chooses the analysis formulation and interprets and records the results; solver runtime itself supplies no labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Analysis cases can repeat measurement, material and cost input entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native import mappings and parameterised cases can reuse actual checked inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Boundary conditions, material behaviour and the validity of any cost-reduction comparison require engineering judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer detects when a result is driven by an invalid assumption rather than a feasible design improvement.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated analysis setup; model and interpretation authority remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: engineering solvers and calculation workbooks can reuse input mappings and case parameters; an executable calculation does not validate its assumptions.

assumptions: Thermal, stress and cost analyses are alternative branches, not mandatory simultaneous tasks; reweight the provisional mix to actual analyses. Boundary ends at checked findings, not physical modifications or procurement.

Measurement producer supplies actual timestamp, value, unit and calibration; designer supplies geometry and material revision; finance or supplier supplies actual cost amount, currency and period where relevant. The engineer validates and manually completes inputs in s1 before case setup. Missing sources or incompatible fields stay manual.
Test native imports and reusable cases before code. Already-imported data and existing solver runtime earn no saving; only actual repeated input entry changes.
Shares and reductions are provisional, not measured baselines. Final save is one percent fully retained and the existing findings check supplies the gate.
unknowns: How much input entry is repeated rather than already linked?
Which analysis branches and boundary conditions are actually used?
research_questions: Can native case reuse reproduce actual prior results with the same source and unit checks?

incremental.description: Maintain input mappings and validate reusable cases after source changes.

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked final solar analysis findings and exact document destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 20*0.50 input assembly + 25*0.40 case entry = 20; minus 1.5 upkeep = 18.5. If only half that entry is eligible, 10 minus 1.5 = 8.5. Methods, interpretation, findings and solver runtime have no claimed cut.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design vacuum tube collectors for solar applications.

steps.what: Define actual vacuum tube collector requirements, materials and operating conditions
outputs: verified vacuum tube collector design constraints

steps.what: Size vacuum tube heat transfer and losses in the engineering calculation system {OTHER}
inputs: verified vacuum tube collector design constraints

steps.what: Design collector geometry and connections in the engineering drawing system {OTHER}
inputs: verified vacuum tube collector design constraints

steps.what: Test actual collector performance and inspect vacuum integrity and thermal behaviour
Check final collector design and record actual development findings and limitations
outputs: checked final collector design and findings

steps.what: Save the checked vacuum tube collector design revision and findings
inputs: checked final collector design and findings
outputs: saved collector design and actual findings

tasks.design: Configure reusable sizing inputs and parametric collector geometry in the engineering systems {OTHER}. The engineer chooses the heat-transfer assumptions and design, performs actual tests and checks the final design and findings before saving; actual prototype fabrication stays with its real producer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Collector variants repeat sizing inputs, tube geometry and connection drawing work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native calculation references and parametric geometry can reuse repeated values and components.
tasks.still_hard: Vacuum loss, heat transfer, thermal expansion and durability must be evaluated against actual materials and tests.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer connects unexpected physical behaviour to a defensible design change.
tasks.altitude: Less variant-entry work; collector design and validation responsibility stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: engineering calculation and drawing tools can reuse parameterised inputs and geometry; collector performance and vacuum integrity still need physical evidence.

assumptions: Boundary includes collector design and the engineer's actual development testing and findings. Prototype maker supplies the actual prototype; neither fabricated availability nor maker labour is treated as free saved engineer time.

The engineer supplies actual tube dimensions, heat demand, climate cases and chosen assumptions in s1-s3; material producer supplies actual property values and revision. Missing inputs are entered manually. Actual test conditions and observations are captured by the engineer in s4 before s5 uses them.

Test native calculation links and reusable geometry before code. Only repeated entry and drawing change; physics judgement in s2-s3 remains in their retained time. Existing solver runtime and already-configured geometry earn no saving.
Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Same-system save has one percent fully retained time and uses the existing final design check.
unknowns: How much sizing and geometry is already parameterised?
Which prototype tests are actually performed by the engineer?
research_questions: Can actual collector variants reuse geometry and input fields without obscuring changed thermal assumptions?

incremental.description: Maintain collector component and calculation parameter references.

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked final collector design and actual findings, exact revision and document destination; changes require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.30 calculation entry + 30*0.40 geometry entry = 18; minus 1 upkeep = 17. With half that repeated entry eligible, 9 minus 1 = 8. Actual tests, design choices, final findings and save action remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The engineer keeps safety, analysis and collector design responsibility while reducing repeated source, calculation and drawing entry.
skills_to_grow: Native engineering case and geometry reuse
role.ambitious_version: Formal decision rights stay unchanged; validate time returned on actual solar engineering revisions.
